source.anchor: Appendix A.1 actual prescribed trajectories, A5 incoming-rate match and A8 reversed event substitution
source.original_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
Define lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta) max(0,<p,grad V(x)-grad V(r)>). For every finite n>=0 and T>=0 there exists rho:Prefix(n,T)->Prefix(n,T) with (rho(t))_i=T-t_(n-1-i). This witness is produced, not assumed. For every y,r,z and t in Prefix(n,T), form the grid a=(0,t_0,...,t_(n-1),T), indexed from0 through n+1. Set post_j=zAt(y,r,z,n,T,t,j) and arrive_j=Phi_(a_(j+1)-a_j)(post_j) for j=0,...,n. Set A=Gamma(y,r,z,n,T,t)(T), the actual terminal state. Form the reversed grid abar=(0,rho(t)_0,...,rho(t)_(n-1),T), set barPost_j=zAt(y,r,R(A),n,T,rho(t),j), and barArrive_j=Phi_(abar_(j+1)-abar_j)(barPost_j).
For every j=0,...,n, barPost_j=R(arrive_(n-j)) and barArrive_j=R(post_(n-j)). Moreover product over i=0,...,n-1 of lambda_r(barArrive_i) equals product over i=0,...,n-1 of lambda_r(arrive_i). The last arrival arrive_n is the actual terminal state and is not one of the n event-rate factors. Reversal on the n+1 arcs is j->n-j; reversal on the n events is i->n-1-i. Per-event rate equality is proved internally; the public conclusion exports the paired states and product equality.
The theorem covers n=0 (one flow arc and empty products equal1), T=0, rank-zero spaces, zero reflection normals and zero rates. No division by a rate or positivity of a prescribed event rate is assumed. The original six analytic assumptions are the only analytic premises; reversal identities, inverse maps, terminal identification and incoming-rate matching are derived from actual producers. The exact unnormalized simplex measure m is retained in the literal interface but is unused in these pointwise deterministic conclusions.
This is the finite-state and incoming-rate component of the Appendix A.1 reversal proof. At a genuine event the right-continuous post-event value reverses to the original incoming value, not the original post-event value. No equality of the two right-continuous trajectories at all times is claimed. Survival time substitution, weighted density equality, stationary invariance, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, actual expected costs, main results and PBPS/SPHMC composition remain separate.

{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
      (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
      (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
        ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let Rec := (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit
    let Hist : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Rec
    let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>
      {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}
    let Prefix : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Type := fun n T => {t : Fin n → ℝ // t ∈ Δ n T}
    let m : (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Measure (Prefix n T) := fun n T =>
      Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val) (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))
    let zAt : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
        S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
    let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
      Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)
    let Path : ℝ≥0 → Type _ := fun T => {s : ℝ≥0 // s ≤ T} → E × E
    let Ψ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Hist n → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T h s =>
        Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun z j => (h j).elim
          (fun a => if a.1 ≤ s.val then Φ y xRef ((s.val - a.1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2 else z)
          (fun _ => z)) z₀
    let Γ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => Ψ y xRef z₀ n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let R : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let rate : E → E × E → ℝ := fun r z =>
      Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V r))
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : ℝ≥0, ∃ rho : Prefix n T → Prefix n T,
      (∀ t : Prefix n T, ∀ i : Fin n, (rho t).val i = (T : ℝ) - t.val i.rev) ∧
      ∀ y r : E, ∀ z : E × E, ∀ t : Prefix n T,
        let grid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t.val) (T : ℝ)
        let post : Fin (n+1) → E × E := zAt y r z n T t
        let arrive : Fin (n+1) → E × E := fun j =>
          Φ y r (grid j.succ - grid j.castSucc) (post j)
        let A : E × E := Γ y r z n T t ⟨T, le_rfl⟩
        let barGrid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (rho t).val) (T : ℝ)
        let barPost : Fin (n+1) → E × E := zAt y r (R A) n T (rho t)
        let barArrive : Fin (n+1) → E × E := fun j =>
          Φ y r (barGrid j.succ - barGrid j.castSucc) (barPost j)
        (∀ j : Fin (n+1), barPost j = R (arrive j.rev) ∧ barArrive j = R (post j.rev)) ∧
        (∏ i : Fin n, rate r (barArrive i.castSucc)) =
          ∏ i : Fin n, rate r (arrive i.castSucc)

blind_reconstruction.text:
# Anonymous theorem reconstruction

Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive group structure and Borel measurable structure. Let V : E → ℝ be twice continuously Fréchet differentiable. Let α,β ∈ ℝ≥0 and η ∈ ℝ. Assume α > 0, α ≤ β, η > 0, βη ≤ 1 and, for every x,v ∈ E,
α‖v‖² ≤ D(DV)(x)[v][v] ≤ β‖v‖².
All derivatives and gradients are over ℝ.

Fix the following local definitions. For y,r ∈ E, put c(y,r) = y − η∇V(r). For every real u and (x,v) ∈ E × E, put
Φ(y,r,u,(x,v)) =
(c(y,r) + cos(u)(x − c(y,r)) + √η sin(u)v,
 −sin(u)/√η (x − c(y,r)) + cos(u)v).
Multiplication of vectors by real coefficients denotes scalar multiplication.

Set d_r(x) = ∇V(x) − ∇V(r) and
S(r,(x,v)) = (x, v − [2⟨v,d_r(x)⟩/‖d_r(x)‖²] d_r(x)).
Real division by zero is zero, so S is the identity when d_r(x) = 0. Nonzero gradient difference is not assumed.

Define Rec = (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit. A left-summand record is a live nonnegative timestamp/state pair; the right summand is a cemetery marker. Define Hist(n) to be the functions from {0,…,n} to Rec.

For n ∈ ℕ and T ∈ ℝ≥0, Δ(n,T) consists of real n-tuples t such that prepending zero gives a strictly increasing sequence and every coordinate is strictly below T. Prefix(n,T) is the subtype of these tuples. For n > 0 this means 0 < t₀ < ⋯ < tₙ₋₁ < T. Prefix(0,T) contains the unique empty tuple, even for T = 0; Prefix(n,0) is empty for n > 0. Define the local measure m(n,T) exactly as Measure.comap of the subtype-value map Prefix(n,T) → (Fin n → ℝ), applied to volume on (Fin n → ℝ). It is unnormalized, does not occur in the conclusion, and supplies no hypothesis.

Fix y,r,z₀,n,T and t ∈ Prefix(n,T). Set g₀ = 0 and gⱼ = tⱼ₋₁ for 1 ≤ j ≤ n. Define zAt(y,r,z₀,n,T,t) on indices j = 0,…,n by the recursion
p₀ = z₀,
pᵢ₊₁ = S(r,Φ(y,r,tᵢ − gᵢ,pᵢ)), for i = 0,…,n−1.
Here pⱼ is its jth value. Define K(y,r,z₀,n,T,t) ∈ Hist(n) to have live record (Real.toNNReal(gⱼ),pⱼ) at index j. Real.toNNReal is the nonnegative part, so on these valid tuples it is simply gⱼ viewed as a nonnegative real.

Define Path(T) to be the functions {s ∈ ℝ≥0 : s ≤ T} → E × E. For arbitrary h ∈ Hist(n), define Ψ(y,r,z₀,n,T,h)(s) by an increasing-index fold through j = 0,…,n, starting with accumulator z₀. A cemetery marker leaves the accumulator unchanged. A live record (a,w) with a > s also leaves it unchanged. A live record with a ≤ s replaces it by Φ(y,r,s − a,w). This subtraction is first in ℝ≥0, hence truncated at zero, and then coerced to ℝ; in the applicable branch it is ordinary nonnegative elapsed time. Thus the last eligible live record in index order determines the result, or the result remains z₀ if none is eligible. General histories need not have ordered timestamps.

Define Γ(y,r,z₀,n,T,t) = Ψ(y,r,z₀,n,T,K(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)). Define R(x,v) = (x,−v) and
rate(r,(x,v)) = √η max(0,⟨v,∇V(x) − ∇V(r)⟩).

The theorem asserts: for every n ∈ ℕ and every T ∈ ℝ≥0, there is a function ρ : Prefix(n,T) → Prefix(n,T) such that, for every valid t and i = 0,…,n−1,
(ρ(t))ᵢ = T − tₙ₋₁₋ᵢ.
For the same ρ, the following hold for every y,r ∈ E, every initial state z ∈ E × E, and every t ∈ Prefix(n,T).

Set the forward grid g = (0,t₀,…,tₙ₋₁,T), indexed 0,…,n+1. For j = 0,…,n, define
pⱼ = zAt(y,r,z,n,T,t)(j),
aⱼ = Φ(y,r,gⱼ₊₁ − gⱼ,pⱼ).
Set A = Γ(y,r,z,n,T,t)(T), evaluating at the final point of the nonnegative closed interval. Set the reversed grid bar g = (0,(ρ(t))₀,…,(ρ(t))ₙ₋₁,T) and, for j = 0,…,n, define
bar pⱼ = zAt(y,r,R(A),n,T,ρ(t))(j),
bar aⱼ = Φ(y,r,bar gⱼ₊₁ − bar gⱼ,bar pⱼ).
In particular, both recursions use the same y,r,V,η, and the reversed recursion starts from R(A).

Then for every j = 0,…,n,
bar pⱼ = R(aₙ₋ⱼ) and bar aⱼ = R(pₙ₋ⱼ),
and moreover
∏ᵢ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹ rate(r,bar aᵢ) = ∏ᵢ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹ rate(r,aᵢ).

The tuple reversal is n−1−i on n coordinates, whereas the state reversal is n−j on n+1 states. The rate products include only arrival indices 0,…,n−1, excluding the final arrival index n. Zero rate factors are allowed and retained; there is no division by a rate. The recursion reflects at interior event times, with no reflection at the terminal endpoint.

When n = 0, both rate products are empty and equal 1. The state identities still concern j = 0: A = Φ(y,r,T,z), bar p₀ = R(A), and bar a₀ = R(z). They also apply when n = T = 0, with zero elapsed time. When T = 0 and n > 0, claims quantified over Prefix(n,T) are vacuous.

All ambient parameters and hypotheses are fixed before n,T are quantified. The function ρ is chosen before y,r,z,t and works uniformly for all of them. Its prescribed coordinate formula uses only n,T,t and uniquely determines it on valid tuples. The constants α and β appear in the assumptions but not in the definitions or final identities. The flow and rate use η as displayed; the reflection uses V and r. No additional numerical constants are quantified. There are no distributional, randomness, integral, measure-preservation, or full-path equality assertions in this conclusion.

This reconstruction uses the anonymous Lean statement and its approved definition context only. The input packet reports compiled = true; I performed no compilation and make no independent compilation or source-fidelity claim.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualEndpointTimeReversal

/-! Actual finite prescribed-state reversal and incoming-rate product for PBPS Appendix A.1.
The original six analytic hypotheses are retained. Incoming/post-event states are
separate; right-continuous trajectories are not identified pointwise at jumps. -/
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualPrescribedStateReversal
open MeasureTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped ContDiff NNReal ENNReal Classical
noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxHeartbeats 2400000

private theorem finite_state_reversal {X : Type*} (n : ℕ)
    (Φ : ℝ → X → X) (S R : X → X)
    (hS : Function.Involutive S) (hR : Function.Involutive R)
    (hRS : ∀ x, R (S x) = S (R x))
    (hInv : ∀ u x, Φ u (Φ (-u) x) = x)
    (hRev : ∀ u x, R (Φ u (R x)) = Φ (-u) x)
    (d : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (post barPost : Fin (n+1) → X)
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin n, post i.succ = S (Φ (d i.castSucc) (post i.castSucc)))
    (hb : ∀ i : Fin n, barPost i.succ = S (Φ (d i.castSucc.rev) (barPost i.castSucc)))
    (hz : barPost 0 = R (Φ (d (Fin.last n)) (post (Fin.last n)))) :
    ∀ j : Fin (n+1),
      barPost j = R (Φ (d j.rev) (post j.rev)) ∧
      Φ (d j.rev) (barPost j) = R (post j.rev) := by
  have hRR (x : X) : R (R x) = x := hR x
  have hSS (x : X) : S (S x) = x := hS x
  have hc (u : ℝ) (x : X) : R (Φ u x) = Φ (-u) (R x) := by
    simpa only [hRR] using hRev u (R x)
  have hcancel (u : ℝ) (x : X) : Φ u (R (Φ u x)) = R x := by
    rw [hc, hInv]
  intro j
  induction j using Fin.induction with
  | zero =>
    constructor
    · simpa only [Fin.rev_zero] using hz
    · rw [hz, Fin.rev_zero, hcancel]
  | succ i ih =>
    have hs : barPost i.succ = R (Φ (d i.succ.rev) (post i.succ.rev)) := by
      rw [hb, ih.2, Fin.rev_castSucc, hp, hRS, hSS, Fin.rev_succ]
    exact ⟨hs, by rw [hs, hcancel]⟩

private theorem incoming_rate_product {X : Type*} (n : ℕ) (S R : X → X)
    (rate : X → ℝ) (hRate : ∀ x, rate (R (S x)) = rate x)
    (post arrive barArrive : Fin (n+1) → X)
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin n, post i.succ = S (arrive i.castSucc))
    (hb : ∀ j : Fin (n+1), barArrive j = R (post j.rev)) :
    (∏ i : Fin n, rate (barArrive i.castSucc)) =
      ∏ i : Fin n, rate (arrive i.castSucc) := by
  have he (i : Fin n) : rate (barArrive i.castSucc) = rate (arrive i.rev.castSucc) := by
    rw [hb, Fin.rev_castSucc, hp, hRate]
  simp_rw [he]
  exact Equiv.prod_comp Fin.revPerm (fun i : Fin n => rate (arrive i.castSucc))


private theorem reversed_grid_gaps (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) (t s : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hs : ∀ i, s i = T - t i.rev) :
    let grid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (Fin.cons 0 t) T
    let barGrid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (Fin.cons 0 s) T
    ∀ j : Fin (n+1),
      barGrid j.succ - barGrid j.castSucc =
        grid j.rev.succ - grid j.rev.castSucc := by
  intro grid barGrid j
  have hl : barGrid j.castSucc = T - grid j.rev.succ := by
    induction j using Fin.cases with
    | zero => simp [grid, barGrid]
    | succ i => simp only [grid, barGrid, Fin.rev_succ, Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.cons_succ, hs]
  have hr : barGrid j.succ = T - grid j.rev.castSucc := by
    induction j using Fin.lastCases with
    | last => simp [grid, barGrid]
    | cast i => simp only [grid, barGrid, Fin.rev_castSucc, Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.cons_succ, hs]
  rw [hl, hr]
  ring

      ∀ y r : E, ∀ z : E × E, ∀ t : Prefix n T,
        let grid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t.val) (T : ℝ)
        let post : Fin (n+1) → E × E := zAt y r z n T t
        let arrive : Fin (n+1) → E × E := fun j =>
          Φ y r (grid j.succ - grid j.castSucc) (post j)
        let A : E × E := Γ y r z n T t ⟨T, le_rfl⟩
        let barGrid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (rho t).val) (T : ℝ)
        let barPost : Fin (n+1) → E × E := zAt y r (R A) n T (rho t)
        let barArrive : Fin (n+1) → E × E := fun j =>
          Φ y r (barGrid j.succ - barGrid j.castSucc) (barPost j)
        (∀ j : Fin (n+1), barPost j = R (arrive j.rev) ∧ barArrive j = R (post j.rev)) ∧
        (∏ i : Fin n, rate r (barArrive i.castSucc)) =
          ∏ i : Fin n, rate r (arrive i.castSucc)


theorem actual_prescribed_state_reversal_and_rate_product
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) : actual_prescribed_state_reversal_statement hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη := by
  unfold actual_prescribed_state_reversal_statement
  intro c Φ S Rec Hist Δ Prefix m zAt K Path Ψ Γ R rate n T
  obtain ⟨rho, hrho, _, _, _, hend, _⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualEndpointTimeReversal.actual_endpoint_time_reversal_laws
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη n T
  obtain ⟨_, _, _, _, _, _, hInv, hS, hR, hRev, hRS, hRate, _⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualPhaseReversalVolume.actual_phase_reversal_volume_laws
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  refine ⟨rho, hrho, ?_⟩
  intro y r z t grid post arrive A barGrid barPost barArrive
  let d : Fin (n+1) → ℝ := fun j => grid j.succ - grid j.castSucc
  have hg : ∀ j : Fin (n+1), barGrid j.succ - barGrid j.castSucc = d j.rev :=
    reversed_grid_gaps n (T : ℝ) t.val (rho t).val (hrho t)
  have hp (i : Fin n) : post i.succ = S r (arrive i.castSucc) := by
    simp only [post, arrive, grid, zAt, Fin.succ_castSucc,
      Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.cons_succ, Fin.induction_succ]
  have hb0 (i : Fin n) : barPost i.succ = S r (barArrive i.castSucc) := by
    simp only [barPost, barArrive, barGrid, zAt, Fin.succ_castSucc,
      Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.cons_succ, Fin.induction_succ]
  have hb (i : Fin n) : barPost i.succ =
      S r (Φ y r (d i.castSucc.rev) (barPost i.castSucc)) := by
    rw [hb0]
    change S r (Φ y r (barGrid i.castSucc.succ - barGrid i.castSucc.castSucc)
      (barPost i.castSucc)) = _
    rw [hg]
  have hz : barPost 0 = R (Φ y r (d (Fin.last n)) (post (Fin.last n))) := by
    change R A = R (arrive (Fin.last n))
    congr 1
    simpa only [arrive, d, grid, post, Fin.succ_last, Fin.snoc_last,
      Fin.snoc_castSucc] using hend y r z t
  have hstates := finite_state_reversal n (Φ y r) (S r) R
    (fun q => hS r q) (fun q => hR q) (fun q => hRS r q)
    (fun u q => (hInv y r u q).2) (fun u q => hRev y r u q)
    d post barPost hp hb hz
  have hpair (j : Fin (n+1)) :
      barPost j = R (arrive j.rev) ∧ barArrive j = R (post j.rev) := by
    refine ⟨(hstates j).1, ?_⟩
    change Φ y r (barGrid j.succ - barGrid j.castSucc) (barPost j) = _
    rw [hg]
    exact (hstates j).2
  refine ⟨hpair, ?_⟩
  exact incoming_rate_product n (S r) R (rate r) (fun q => hRate r q)
    post arrive barArrive hp (fun j => (hpair j).2)

#print axioms actual_prescribed_state_reversal_and_rate_product
end
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualPrescribedStateReversal

Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
Define lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta) max(0,<p,grad V(x)-grad V(r)>). For every finite n>=0 and T>=0 there exists rho:Prefix(n,T)->Prefix(n,T) with (rho(t))_i=T-t_(n-1-i). This witness is produced, not assumed. For every y,r,z and t in Prefix(n,T), form the grid a=(0,t_0,...,t_(n-1),T), indexed from0 through n+1. Set post_j=zAt(y,r,z,n,T,t,j) and arrive_j=Phi_(a_(j+1)-a_j)(post_j) for j=0,...,n. Set A=Gamma(y,r,z,n,T,t)(T), the actual terminal state. Form the reversed grid abar=(0,rho(t)_0,...,rho(t)_(n-1),T), set barPost_j=zAt(y,r,R(A),n,T,rho(t),j), and barArrive_j=Phi_(abar_(j+1)-abar_j)(barPost_j).
For every j=0,...,n, barPost_j=R(arrive_(n-j)) and barArrive_j=R(post_(n-j)). Moreover product over i=0,...,n-1 of lambda_r(barArrive_i) equals product over i=0,...,n-1 of lambda_r(arrive_i). The last arrival arrive_n is the actual terminal state and is not one of the n event-rate factors. Reversal on the n+1 arcs is j->n-j; reversal on the n events is i->n-1-i. Per-event rate equality is proved internally; the public conclusion exports the paired states and product equality.
The theorem covers n=0 (one flow arc and empty products equal1), T=0, rank-zero spaces, zero reflection normals and zero rates. No division by a rate or positivity of a prescribed event rate is assumed. The original six analytic assumptions are the only analytic premises; reversal identities, inverse maps, terminal identification and incoming-rate matching are derived from actual producers. The exact unnormalized simplex measure m is retained in the literal interface but is unused in these pointwise deterministic conclusions.
This is the finite-state and incoming-rate component of the Appendix A.1 reversal proof. At a genuine event the right-continuous post-event value reverses to the original incoming value, not the original post-event value. No equality of the two right-continuous trajectories at all times is claimed. Survival time substitution, weighted density equality, stationary invariance, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, actual expected costs, main results and PBPS/SPHMC composition remain separate.

steps.title: Reverse each finite incoming and post-event state
steps.text: The private finite-array lemma first combines momentum reversal with the inverse flow to obtain Phi_u(R(Phi_u q))=R q. The reversed initial state is the reversal of the final arrival. Induct over reversed events. The flow identity turns the paired reversed post-state into the reversal of the original post-state. The next reversed bounce is S R S applied to the original arrival, which equals R because S is involutive and commutes with R. The Fin casts convert arc reversal into event reversal exactly. These algebraic premises are internal and are supplied by actual PBPS laws below.
steps.lean:
private theorem finite_state_reversal {X : Type*} (n : ℕ)
    (Φ : ℝ → X → X) (S R : X → X)
    (hS : Function.Involutive S) (hR : Function.Involutive R)
    (hRS : ∀ x, R (S x) = S (R x))
    (hInv : ∀ u x, Φ u (Φ (-u) x) = x)
    (hRev : ∀ u x, R (Φ u (R x)) = Φ (-u) x)
    (d : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (post barPost : Fin (n+1) → X)
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin n, post i.succ = S (Φ (d i.castSucc) (post i.castSucc)))
    (hb : ∀ i : Fin n, barPost i.succ = S (Φ (d i.castSucc.rev) (barPost i.castSucc)))
    (hz : barPost 0 = R (Φ (d (Fin.last n)) (post (Fin.last n)))) :
    ∀ j : Fin (n+1),
      barPost j = R (Φ (d j.rev) (post j.rev)) ∧
      Φ (d j.rev) (barPost j) = R (post j.rev) := by
  have hRR (x : X) : R (R x) = x := hR x
  have hSS (x : X) : S (S x) = x := hS x
  have hc (u : ℝ) (x : X) : R (Φ u x) = Φ (-u) (R x) := by
    simpa only [hRR] using hRev u (R x)
  have hcancel (u : ℝ) (x : X) : Φ u (R (Φ u x)) = R x := by
    rw [hc, hInv]
  intro j
  induction j using Fin.induction with
  | zero =>
    constructor
    · simpa only [Fin.rev_zero] using hz
    · rw [hz, Fin.rev_zero, hcancel]
  | succ i ih =>
    have hs : barPost i.succ = R (Φ (d i.succ.rev) (post i.succ.rev)) := by
      rw [hb, ih.2, Fin.rev_castSucc, hp, hRS, hSS, Fin.rev_succ]
    exact ⟨hs, by rw [hs, hcancel]⟩

steps.title: Pair incoming event rates and permute the finite product
steps.text: At reversed event i, the state identity gives barArrive_i=R(post_(n-i))=R(S(arrive_(n-1-i))). The actual rate identity lambda(R S q)=lambda(q) pairs the corresponding incoming rates. Apply the permutation Fin.rev to reindex the product. No factor is cancelled, so zero rates are included; with no events both products are1. The individual rate pairing is an internal step, while the public result exposes the product.
steps.lean:
private theorem incoming_rate_product {X : Type*} (n : ℕ) (S R : X → X)
    (rate : X → ℝ) (hRate : ∀ x, rate (R (S x)) = rate x)
    (post arrive barArrive : Fin (n+1) → X)
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin n, post i.succ = S (arrive i.castSucc))
    (hb : ∀ j : Fin (n+1), barArrive j = R (post j.rev)) :
    (∏ i : Fin n, rate (barArrive i.castSucc)) =
      ∏ i : Fin n, rate (arrive i.castSucc) := by
  have he (i : Fin n) : rate (barArrive i.castSucc) = rate (arrive i.rev.castSucc) := by
    rw [hb, Fin.rev_castSucc, hp, hRate]
  simp_rw [he]
  exact Equiv.prod_comp Fin.revPerm (fun i : Fin n => rate (arrive i.castSucc))

steps.title: Match the lengths of reversed flow arcs
steps.text: Prepend zero and append T to both event tuples. The coordinate equation rho(t)_i=T-t_(n-1-i) gives abar_j=T-a_(n+1-j) and abar_(j+1)=T-a_(n-j). Subtract to obtain the original arc length at index n-j. The first and last grid entries are checked separately by finite cases, so the one-arc n=0 case remains valid. This is an adapter for the actual grid representation; it invokes no private declaration from another module.
steps.lean:
private theorem reversed_grid_gaps (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) (t s : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hs : ∀ i, s i = T - t i.rev) :
    let grid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (Fin.cons 0 t) T
    let barGrid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (Fin.cons 0 s) T
    ∀ j : Fin (n+1),
      barGrid j.succ - barGrid j.castSucc =
        grid j.rev.succ - grid j.rev.castSucc := by
  intro grid barGrid j
  have hl : barGrid j.castSucc = T - grid j.rev.succ := by
    induction j using Fin.cases with
    | zero => simp [grid, barGrid]
    | succ i => simp only [grid, barGrid, Fin.rev_succ, Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.cons_succ, hs]
  have hr : barGrid j.succ = T - grid j.rev.castSucc := by
    induction j using Fin.lastCases with
    | last => simp [grid, barGrid]
    | cast i => simp only [grid, barGrid, Fin.rev_castSucc, Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.cons_succ, hs]
  rw [hl, hr]
  ring

steps.title: Assemble the actual state and incoming-product conclusions
steps.text: Invoke finite state reversal with the actual harmonic flow, bounce, momentum reversal and proved recurrences. Re-express its reversed-length flow as the literal barArrive array using the grid identity. This proves both state equalities. Supply the actual rate identity and state equalities to the finite-product lemma to obtain the product conclusion. The proof keeps incoming and post-event states separate; path reversal away from events and survival-integral substitution are later dependencies.

have hstates := finite_state_reversal n (Φ y r) (S r) R
    (fun q => hS r q) (fun q => hR q) (fun q => hRS r q)
    (fun u q => (hInv y r u q).2) (fun u q => hRev y r u q)
    d post barPost hp hb hz
  have hpair (j : Fin (n+1)) :
      barPost j = R (arrive j.rev) ∧ barArrive j = R (post j.rev) := by
    refine ⟨(hstates j).1, ?_⟩
    change Φ y r (barGrid j.succ - barGrid j.castSucc) (barPost j) = _
    rw [hg]
    exact (hstates j).2
  refine ⟨hpair, ?_⟩
  exact incoming_rate_product n (S r) R (rate r) (fun q => hRate r q)
    post arrive barArrive hp (fun j => (hpair j).2)

lesson.lean_statement:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
Define lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta) max(0,<p,grad V(x)-grad V(r)>). For every finite n>=0 and T>=0 there exists rho:Prefix(n,T)->Prefix(n,T) with (rho(t))_i=T-t_(n-1-i). This witness is produced, not assumed. For every y,r,z and t in Prefix(n,T), form the grid a=(0,t_0,...,t_(n-1),T), indexed from0 through n+1. Set post_j=zAt(y,r,z,n,T,t,j) and arrive_j=Phi_(a_(j+1)-a_j)(post_j) for j=0,...,n. Set A=Gamma(y,r,z,n,T,t)(T), the actual terminal state. Form the reversed grid abar=(0,rho(t)_0,...,rho(t)_(n-1),T), set barPost_j=zAt(y,r,R(A),n,T,rho(t),j), and barArrive_j=Phi_(abar_(j+1)-abar_j)(barPost_j).
For every j=0,...,n, barPost_j=R(arrive_(n-j)) and barArrive_j=R(post_(n-j)). Moreover product over i=0,...,n-1 of lambda_r(barArrive_i) equals product over i=0,...,n-1 of lambda_r(arrive_i). The last arrival arrive_n is the actual terminal state and is not one of the n event-rate factors. Reversal on the n+1 arcs is j->n-j; reversal on the n events is i->n-1-i. Per-event rate equality is proved internally; the public conclusion exports the paired states and product equality.
The theorem covers n=0 (one flow arc and empty products equal1), T=0, rank-zero spaces, zero reflection normals and zero rates. No division by a rate or positivity of a prescribed event rate is assumed. The original six analytic assumptions are the only analytic premises; reversal identities, inverse maps, terminal identification and incoming-rate matching are derived from actual producers. The exact unnormalized simplex measure m is retained in the literal interface but is unused in these pointwise deterministic conclusions.
This is the finite-state and incoming-rate component of the Appendix A.1 reversal proof. At a genuine event the right-continuous post-event value reverses to the original incoming value, not the original post-event value. No equality of the two right-continuous trajectories at all times is claimed. Survival time substitution, weighted density equality, stationary invariance, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, actual expected costs, main results and PBPS/SPHMC composition remain separate.
